Empirical Research Plan – Cash Transfers and Political Support in Uruguay

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Primary method: Fuzzy Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)

Rationale  
• Eligibility for the transfer is a deterministic step function of a welfare‐index score (running variable).  
• Not all eligible individuals may enroll and a few ineligibles may still obtain benefits → first-stage “jump” in treatment probability, not a perfect discontinuity → fuzzy RD.  
• RDD is the closest quasi-experiment here: individuals infinitesimally on either side of the cutoff are plausibly identical in expectations except for a large difference in treatment probability.  
Supplementary analyses  
• RD-in-Time (RDD × pre/post) or RDDD can be used to test pre-election vs. post-election effects.  
• Event-study style graphs of vote shares across the welfare-index score allow visual confirmation.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control Definition
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Di = 1 if individual i actually received the cash transfer in the period preceding the 2004 election; 0 otherwise.

Running variable and cutoff  
Si = household welfare-index score (lower values = poorer).  
Cutoff c = program eligibility threshold (administratively fixed; e.g. c = 14, but exact value taken from the law).  

Treatment timing  
• Treatment is measured in the 12 months before the Oct-2004 national election.  
• Outcome (political support) is “voted for incumbent party in 2004” (binary).  

Control group / counterfactual  
Individuals with Si just above c (ineligible or less likely to receive) supply the counterfactual political support level.  

Bandwidth  
Use data-driven bandwidth selectors (Calonico-Cattaneo-Titiunik) and show robustness to ±25%, ±50% of optimal h.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes  
Without the transfer, the probability of voting for the incumbent varies smoothly in Si at c.  
Plausibility: score is a composite administrative index; difficult for citizens to fine-tune exactly; no concurrent political program tied precisely to the same cutoff.

A2. No precise manipulation of running variable around c  
Individuals/firms cannot perfectly sort across the threshold.  
Plausibility: index built from lagged income, assets; spot checks; manipulation costly. Test: McCrary density test + covariate balance.

A3. First-stage relevance (discontinuity in treatment probability)  
Pr(Di =1) jumps at c. Plausible by construction; verify empirically.

A4. Local Stable Unit Treatment Value Assumption (no spillovers within bandwidth)  
Receiving transfer does not directly alter neighbors’ voting within very small bandwidth.  
Plausible: voting is private; information spillovers likely low at narrow margins.

A5. Monotonicity (for fuzzy RD as IV)  
Crossing the cutoff weakly increases probability of treatment for everyone (no “defiers”).  
Plausible; incentives only go one way.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Score manipulation / sorting  
• Perform McCrary test; show continuity in predetermined covariates.  
• Narrower bandwidths; donut RD (drop ±1 point around c).  

T2. Other policies keyed to same index  
• Collect data on all social programs; control for any that also use Si.  
• Or implement RD-differences: compare change in incumbent vote share 2004 vs. 1999 across the cutoff.

T3. Differential turnout vs. vote choice  
If transfer affects turnout rather than partisan choice, interpretation blurs.  
• Estimate two stages: (i) turnout, (ii) conditional vote choice.  
• Use administrative turnout records to separate effects.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(rdrobust)     # RD estimation
library(fixest)       # OLS & IV within bandwidth
library(rddensity)    # McCrary test

# 1. Load data  -------------------------------------------------------------
dat <- read_csv("uruguay_cash_transfer_elec.csv")

# 2. Variable construction --------------------------------------------------
dat <- dat %>% 
  mutate(
    running      = welfare_index,          # Si
    treat_actual = as.numeric(transfer==1),
    elig         = as.numeric(running <= cutoff_value), # running low = eligible
    vote_incumb  = as.numeric(vote=="incumbent"),
    post2004     = as.numeric(year==2004)  # for RDDD robustness
  )

# 3. Descriptive balance & manipulation test --------------------------------
# McCrary density
dc <- rddensity(X = dat$running, c = cutoff_value)
summary(dc)

# Covariate balance within ±2 score points
balance_bw <- 2
bal_dat <- dat %>% filter(abs(running - cutoff_value) <= balance_bw)
lm(age ~ elig, data = bal_dat) %>% summary()

# 4. Main fuzzy RD  ---------------------------------------------------------
# Optimal bandwidth
rd_out <- rdrobust(y = dat$vote_incumb,
                   x = dat$running,
                   c = cutoff_value,
                   fuzzy = dat$treat_actual)

summary(rd_out)  # Wald estimate = Local Average Treatment Effect

# 5. Alternative spec: IV via fixest within bandwidth -----------------------
bw <- rd_bw_ik(dat$running, cutoff_value)  # Imbens–Kalyanaraman rule
local <- dat %>% filter(abs(running - cutoff_value) <= bw)

iv_est <- feols(vote_incumb ~ 1 | treat_actual ~ elig,
                data = local,
                se = "hc3")
summary(iv_est)

# 6. Robustness check: Donut RD (drop ±0.3 around c) ------------------------
donut <- dat %>% filter(abs(running - cutoff_value) > 0.3 & 
                        abs(running - cutoff_value) <= bw)
rd_donut <- rdrobust(y = donut$vote_incumb,
                     x = donut$running,
                     c = cutoff_value,
                     fuzzy = donut$treat_actual)
summary(rd_donut)
```

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Theory and previous literature suggest transfers raise gratitude and reciprocity toward incumbents.  
Prior: a positive effect of roughly 4–8 percentage points in incumbent vote share among compliers at the cutoff. Turnout may also rise slightly.  

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RD)  
(1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable)

C1: Large, discontinuous jump in treatment probability at cutoff …… 1  
C2: Smooth density of running variable at cutoff (no manipulation) … 0.8 (to be tested)  
C3: Covariates continuous at cutoff ………………………………………… 0.9  
C4: No other discontinuous policies at same cutoff …………………… 0.7  
C5: Sufficient observations within optimal bandwidth ……………… 1  

Total ≈ 4.4 / 5 → credible but still requires robustness checks detailed above.
